title: The category of coherent formal modules is abelian
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Then the category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] is abelian [def-sp-abelian]; the cokernel of a morphism $\alpha=(\alpha_n):(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ is the inverse system $(\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n)_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian), part (1), and the description of cokernels in its proof

proof.text: (Preliminaries.) Let $(\mathcal F_n)$ be an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Each transition map $\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ is surjective (it induces $\mathcal F_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}\cong\mathcal F_n$), so for $l\ge m$ the composite $\mathcal F_l\to\mathcal F_m$ is an epimorphism, and it induces an isomorphism $\mathcal F_l/\mathcal I^m\mathcal F_l\cong\mathcal F_m$ (induction on $l$: $\mathcal F_l/\mathcal I^m\mathcal F_l\cong(\mathcal F_l/\mathcal I^{l-1}\mathcal F_l)/\mathcal I^m(\ldots)\cong\mathcal F_{l-1}/\mathcal I^m\mathcal F_{l-1}$ for $m\le l-1$, as $\mathcal I^{l-1}\subseteq\mathcal I^m$; on the $U_j$ below this is $p_m$ having kernel $I_j^mM\supseteq I_j^lM$). A morphism $(\alpha_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ all of whose components are isomorphisms is an isomorphism (the inverses $\alpha_n^{-1}$ commute with the transition maps). Since $X$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] with quasi-compact underlying space) choose a finite covering $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_r$ by affine opens $U_j\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ with $A_j$ Noetherian. Every quasi-coherent $\mathcal G$ satisfies $\mathcal G|_{U_j}\cong\widetilde{\mathcal G(U_j)}$ naturally (counit isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3)); hence a morphism of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules is an isomorphism (resp. zero) as soon as it is bijective (resp. zero) on $U_j$-sections for every $j$ (an isomorphism of sheaves is local on $X$), and two quasi-coherent submodules of a module with the same $U_j$-sections for all $j$, one contained in the other, are equal. In particular $\mathcal I|_{U_j}=\widetilde{I_j}$ with $I_j=\mathcal I(U_j)$, and $\mathcal I^n(U_j)=I_j^n$, $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal G)(U_j)=I_j^n\mathcal G(U_j)$, $(\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n\mathcal G)(U_j)=\mathcal G(U_j)/I_j^n\mathcal G(U_j)$ for quasi-coherent $\mathcal G$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1),(2). By (3) of that node and since coherence is local, $(\mathcal F_n|_{U})$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$ for every open $U$, and restriction is a functor $\rho_U$. For $U=U_j$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (1): $M=\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n(U_j)$ is a finitely generated $A_j^\wedge$-module ($A_j^\wedge$ the $I_j$-adic completion) and $p_n:M\to\mathcal F_n(U_j)$ is surjective with kernel $I_j^nM$; for a morphism $\alpha:(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$, with $N=\varprojlim_n\mathcal G_n(U_j)$, the map $f=\varprojlim_n\alpha_n(U_j):M\to N$ is $A_j^\wedge$-linear and $\alpha_n(U_j)\circ p_n=p_n\circ f$, i.e. $\alpha_n(U_j)$ is $f\bmod I_j^n:M/I_j^nM\to N/I_j^nN$. These identifications are used below without mention (\"on $U_j$\").

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian, line 6313): 'To see (a), (b), and (c) we may work affine locally, say X = Spec(A) ... By Lemma 087W alpha corresponds to a map f : M -> N of finite A^-modules'; Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine, line 6272) and its proof

proof.text: (Additive structure.) For objects $(\mathcal F_n),(\mathcal G_n)$ the morphisms form an abelian group under termwise addition $(\alpha_n)+(\beta_n)=(\alpha_n+\beta_n)$ (sums of maps commuting with the transition maps commute with them), and composition is bilinear; the system $(0)_n$ is a zero object. The termwise direct sum $(\mathcal F_n\oplus\mathcal G_n)$ with the direct sums of the transition maps is an object: $\mathcal F_n\oplus\mathcal G_n$ is coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] (1), and $\mathcal I^n(\mathcal F\oplus\mathcal G)=\mathcal I^n\mathcal F\oplus\mathcal I^n\mathcal G$ (check on the $U_j$-sections by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2), where it is $I_j^n(P\oplus Q)=I_j^nP\oplus I_j^nQ$), so $\mathcal I^n$ kills $\mathcal F_n\oplus\mathcal G_n$ and $(\mathcal F_{n+1}\oplus\mathcal G_{n+1})/\mathcal I^n(\ldots)\cong\mathcal F_n\oplus\mathcal G_n$. With the termwise inclusions and projections it is a biproduct in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ (the identities of a biproduct hold termwise). So $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is preadditive with finite products.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Section 087V (section-existence, line 6255: 'A morphism of such inverse systems is defined as usual'); the additive structure is not written out in Stacks (written by the agent)

proof.text: (Cokernels are termwise.) Let $\alpha=(\alpha_n):(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ and let $q_n:\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal C_n=\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n$ be the cokernel in $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]; $\mathcal C_n$ is coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] (1), and the transition maps of $(\mathcal G_n)$ induce transition maps $\mathcal C_{n+1}\to\mathcal C_n$ (as $\alpha$ commutes with the transition maps). On $U_j$: $\mathcal C_n(U_j)=\mathcal G_n(U_j)/\alpha_n(\mathcal F_n(U_j))$ ([lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (3)), so $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal C_n)(U_j)=I_j^n\mathcal C_n(U_j)=0$ (it is the image of $I_j^n\mathcal G_n(U_j)=0$) and $\mathcal I^n\mathcal C_n=0$ (Step 1). The map $\mathcal C_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal C_{n+1}\to\mathcal C_n$ is on $U_j$-sections the map $\mathcal G_{n+1}(U_j)/(\alpha_{n+1}(\mathcal F_{n+1}(U_j))+I_j^n\mathcal G_{n+1}(U_j))\to\mathcal G_n(U_j)/\alpha_n(\mathcal F_n(U_j))$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2), which is bijective because $\mathcal G_{n+1}(U_j)\to\mathcal G_n(U_j)$ is surjective with kernel $I_j^n\mathcal G_{n+1}(U_j)$ and $\mathcal F_{n+1}(U_j)\to\mathcal F_n(U_j)$ is surjective (Step 1); hence it is an isomorphism (Step 1) and $(\mathcal C_n)$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, $q=(q_n)$ a morphism with $q\circ\alpha=0$. If $\beta:(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal H_n)$ satisfies $\beta\circ\alpha=0$, each $\beta_n$ factors uniquely as $\beta_n=\bar\beta_n\circ q_n$, and the $\bar\beta_n$ commute with the transition maps because they do so after composing with the epimorphism $q_{n+1}$. So $q:(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal C_n)$ is a cokernel of $\alpha$ in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$; this proves the cokernel clause of the statement and the existence of cokernels.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087X: 'The cokernel of alpha is the inverse system (Coker(alpha_n)) (details omitted)'; the omitted details are written out by the agent

proof.text: (Kernels, claim (a): stabilization by Artin-Rees.) Let $\alpha:(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$. For $l\ge m$ let $\mathcal K'_{l,m}\subseteq\mathcal F_m$ be the image of the composite $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_l\subseteq\mathcal F_l\to\mathcal F_m$. As $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_l$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel], $\mathcal K'_{l,m}$ is a quasi-coherent submodule of $\mathcal F_m$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (1),(2), hence coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] (2); and $\mathcal K'_{l+1,m}\subseteq\mathcal K'_{l,m}$ since $\mathcal F_{l+1}\to\mathcal F_l$ maps $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_{l+1}$ into $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_l$. Fix $j$ and let $M,N,f$ be as in Step 1 for $U_j$, $I=I_j$, $K=\operatorname{Ker}f$. Kernels are sectionwise, so $(\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_l)(U_j)=p_l(f^{-1}(I^lN))$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (3) $\mathcal K'_{l,m}(U_j)=p_m(f^{-1}(I^lN))=(f^{-1}(I^lN)+I^mM)/I^mM$. The ring $A_j^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], so $K\subseteq M$ and $f(M)\subseteq N$ are finitely generated, and the Artin-Rees lemma [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] over $A_j^\wedge$ for the ideal $IA_j^\wedge$ (note $(IA_j^\wedge)^nM=I^nM$), applied to $K\subseteq M$ and to $f(M)\subseteq N$, gives $c_j\ge0$ with $K\cap I^nM\subseteq I^{n-c_j}K$ and $f(M)\cap I^nN\subseteq I^{n-c_j}f(M)=f(I^{n-c_j}M)$ for all $n\ge c_j$. Consequently $f^{-1}(I^lN)\subseteq K+I^{l-c_j}M$ for $l\ge c_j$ (if $f(x)\in I^lN$, then $f(x)=f(y)$ with $y\in I^{l-c_j}M$, and $x-y\in K$). Put $c=\max_jc_j$; both inclusions hold with $c$ in place of $c_j$. For $l\ge m+c$ we get $K\subseteq f^{-1}(I^lN)\subseteq K+I^mM$, hence $\mathcal K'_{l,m}(U_j)=(K+I^mM)/I^mM$ for every $j$, so $\mathcal K'_{l,m}=\mathcal K'_{m+c,m}$ (Step 1). Write $\mathcal K'_m=\mathcal K'_{m+c,m}$; it is the constant value of the decreasing system $(\mathcal K'_{l,m})_{l\ge m}$, and $\mathcal K'_m(U_j)=(K+I^mM)/I^mM\cong K/(K\cap I^mM)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087X, claim (a) and the computation of K'_{l,m}; Stacks chooses c by Algebra, Lemma 00IN (lemma-Artin-Rees) and Lemma 00IO (lemma-map-AR, whose proof is 00IN applied to Im(f) in N, done here directly); Stacks writes 'a^{-1}(I^lN)' for f^{-1}(I^lN) (typo); A^ Noetherian by Algebra, Lemma 0316

proof.text: (Kernels, claims (b) and (c).) For $m'\ge m$ the transition $\mathcal F_{m'}\to\mathcal F_m$ maps $\mathcal K'_{l,m'}$ into $\mathcal K'_{l,m}$ (the composite $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_l\to\mathcal F_{m'}\to\mathcal F_m$ is the map defining $\mathcal K'_{l,m}$), hence induces $\tau:\mathcal K'_{m'}\to\mathcal K'_m$, which on $U_j$ is the map $(K+I^{m'}M)/I^{m'}M\to(K+I^mM)/I^mM$ induced by the identity. By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1),(2), $\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_m$ is quasi-coherent and $(\mathcal K'_m/\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_m)(U_j)=K/(K\cap I^mM+I^nK)$, which equals $K/I^nK$ when $m\ge n+c$ because then $K\cap I^mM\subseteq I^{m-c}K\subseteq I^nK$ (Step 4). Hence for $m'\ge m\ge n+c$ the map $\mathcal K'_{m'}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_{m'}\to\mathcal K'_m/\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_m$ induced by $\tau$ is on every $U_j$ the identity of $K/I^nK$, so an isomorphism (Step 1): the system $(\mathcal K'_m/\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_m)_{m\ge n}$ is constant from $m=n+c$ on (claim (b)). Put $\mathcal K_n=\mathcal K'_{n+c}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_{n+c}$, with transition maps $\mathcal K_{n+1}\to\mathcal K_n$ induced by $\tau:\mathcal K'_{n+1+c}\to\mathcal K'_{n+c}$ (which maps $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal K'_{n+1+c}$ into $\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_{n+c}$). $\mathcal K_n$ is coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] (2) (quotient of the coherent $\mathcal K'_{n+c}$ by a quasi-coherent submodule); $\mathcal I^n\mathcal K_n=0$ and $\mathcal K_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal K_{n+1}\to\mathcal K_n$ is an isomorphism, since on $U_j$ these are $I^n(K/I^nK)=0$ and the canonical bijection $(K/I^{n+1}K)/I^n(K/I^{n+1}K)\to K/I^nK$ (Step 1). So $(\mathcal K_n)$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ (claim (c)), with $\mathcal K_n(U_j)=K/I^nK$ compatibly with the transition maps.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087X, claims (b), (c) and the computation 'K'_m/I^nK'_m corresponds to K/(K cap I^mM + I^nK) = K/I^nK for m >= n + c'

proof.text: (Kernels, claim (d): the factorization exists.) Let $\iota_n:\mathcal K_n\to\mathcal F_n$ be induced by the inclusion $\mathcal K'_{n+c}\subseteq\mathcal F_{n+c}$ and $\mathcal F_{n+c}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+c}\cong\mathcal F_n$; on $U_j$ it is the map $K/I^nK\to M/I^nM$ induced by $K\subseteq M$, so $\iota=(\iota_n)$ commutes with the transition maps and $\alpha\circ\iota=0$ ($f(K)=0$; Step 1). Let $\beta:(\mathcal H_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)$ with $\alpha\circ\beta=0$. For $l\ge m$, $\beta_l(\mathcal H_l)\subseteq\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_l$ and $(\mathcal F_l\to\mathcal F_m)\circ\beta_l=\beta_m\circ(\mathcal H_l\to\mathcal H_m)$; since $\mathcal H_l\to\mathcal H_m$ is an epimorphism (Step 1), the image of $\beta_m$ is the image of $(\mathcal F_l\to\mathcal F_m)\circ\beta_l$, contained in $\mathcal K'_{l,m}$. Taking $l=m+c$, $\beta_m$ factors as $\mathcal H_m\xrightarrow{\beta'_m}\mathcal K'_m\subseteq\mathcal F_m$. The map $\beta'_{n+c}$ sends $\mathcal I^n\mathcal H_{n+c}$ into $\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_{n+c}$ and so induces $\gamma_n:\mathcal H_n\cong\mathcal H_{n+c}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal H_{n+c}\to\mathcal K_n$. Both $\iota_n\circ\gamma_n$ and $\beta_n$ are the reduction modulo $\mathcal I^n$ of $\beta_{n+c}$ (as $\beta$ commutes with the transition maps), so $\iota_n\circ\gamma_n=\beta_n$; and $\gamma$ commutes with the transition maps, both composites $\mathcal H_{n+1}\to\mathcal K_n$ being the reduction modulo $\mathcal I^n$ of $\tau\circ\beta'_{n+1+c}=\beta'_{n+c}\circ(\mathcal H_{n+1+c}\to\mathcal H_{n+c})$ (equal after composing with the inclusion $\mathcal K'_{n+c}\subseteq\mathcal F_{n+c}$).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087X, proof of (d): 'Then H_l -> F_l maps into Ker(alpha_l) ... we obtain a system of maps H_m -> K'_{l,m} ... and hence a map H_n -> K_n as desired'

proof.text: (Kernels: uniqueness of the factorization.) Let $\gamma:(\mathcal H_n)\to(\mathcal K_n)$ with $\iota\circ\gamma=0$; we show $\gamma=0$, so the factorization of Step 6 is unique (apply this to the difference of two factorizations). The sheaf $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Ker}\iota_{n+c}$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] with $\mathcal P(U_j)=\operatorname{Ker}(K/I^{n+c}K\to M/I^{n+c}M)=(K\cap I^{n+c}M)/I^{n+c}K\subseteq I^nK/I^{n+c}K$ by the Artin-Rees inclusion of Step 4 [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees]; the transition $\mathcal K_{n+c}\to\mathcal K_n$, on $U_j$ the projection $K/I^{n+c}K\to K/I^nK$, vanishes on these sections, so its restriction to $\mathcal P$ is zero (Step 1). As $\gamma_{n+c}(\mathcal H_{n+c})\subseteq\mathcal P$, we get $\gamma_n\circ(\mathcal H_{n+c}\to\mathcal H_n)=(\mathcal K_{n+c}\to\mathcal K_n)\circ\gamma_{n+c}=0$, and since $\mathcal H_{n+c}\to\mathcal H_n$ is an epimorphism, $\gamma_n=0$. Hence $\iota:(\mathcal K_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)$ is a kernel of $\alpha$ in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, and $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ has kernels. (The termwise maps $\iota_n$ need not be injective: $K\cap I^nM\ne I^nK$ in general.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087X, (d); Stacks proves only the existence of the factorization, the uniqueness is written by the agent from the same Artin-Rees choice of c

proof.text: (Restriction to the affine pieces preserves kernels and cokernels.) Fix $j$. The restriction functor $\rho_j=\rho_{U_j}:\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)\to\mathit{Coh}(U_j,\mathcal I|_{U_j})$ (Step 1; $U_j$ is a Noetherian scheme) is additive. It carries the cokernel of Step 3 to the cokernel of $\rho_j(\alpha)$ built by Step 3 on $U_j$ (cokernels of $\mathcal O_X$-modules restrict to cokernels), and the kernel of Steps 4-7 to the kernel of $\rho_j(\alpha)$ built on $U_j$ (with the covering $\{U_j\}$ and a constant $c'\ge c_j$): kernels, images [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] and products $\mathcal I^n(-)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (3) commute with restriction, so $\mathcal K'_{l,m}|_{U_j}$ is the corresponding module on $U_j$, and by the stabilizations of Steps 4 and 5 both constructions may be taken with $\max(c,c')$. Let $E_j:\mathit{Coh}(U_j,\mathcal I|_{U_j})\to\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(A_j^\wedge)$ be the equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2). In $\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(A_j^\wedge)$ the module kernel and cokernel of an $A_j^\wedge$-linear $f:M\to N$ are finitely generated ($A_j^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]) and are its kernel and cokernel there; an equivalence of categories preserves kernels and cokernels. Hence $\Phi_j=E_j\circ\rho_j$ is an additive functor carrying the kernel and the cokernel of $\alpha$ to $\operatorname{Ker}f\to M$ and $N\to N/f(M)$, where $f=E_j(\rho_j\alpha)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087X, last paragraph: 'taking kernels and cokernels commutes, over affines, with the description of Coh(X, I) as a category of modules' and 'Parts (2) and (3) of the lemma are immediate from our construction of kernels and cokernels'

proof.text: (Coimage equals image.) For $\alpha:(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ let $\operatorname{Coim}\alpha=\operatorname{Coker}(\iota)$, $\operatorname{Im}\alpha=\operatorname{Ker}(q)$ (Steps 3-7) and $\theta:\operatorname{Coim}\alpha\to\operatorname{Im}\alpha$ the canonical morphism. Since $\Phi_j$ is additive and preserves kernels and cokernels (Step 8), it carries $\theta$ to the canonical map $\operatorname{Coim}f=M/\operatorname{Ker}f\to\operatorname{Ker}(N\to N/f(M))=f(M)$ of $A_j^\wedge$-modules, which is bijective (first isomorphism theorem). An equivalence reflects isomorphisms, so $\rho_j(\theta)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathit{Coh}(U_j,\mathcal I|_{U_j})$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2), hence every component $\theta_n|_{U_j}$ is an isomorphism of sheaves. As the $U_j$ cover $X$, every $\theta_n$ is an isomorphism, and $\theta$ is an isomorphism (Step 1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087X, last paragraph: 'To finish the proof of (1) we still have to show that Coim = Im ... Since Im = Coim holds in the category of modules this gives Coim = Im in Coh(X, I)'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is preadditive with finite products (Step 2), has cokernels (Step 3) and kernels (Steps 4-7), and the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Coim}\alpha\to\operatorname{Im}\alpha$ is an isomorphism for every morphism $\alpha$ (Step 9). By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-of-coimage-image-iso] it is an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and by Step 3 the cokernel of $\alpha$ is $(\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n)_n$.
